dish: Okinawa zenzai (brown-sugar-simmered beans under a mound of shaved ice)
w: Naha's classic zenzai parlour near Naminoue Shrine, in business since the 1950s (the founders' Yafune Shokudo, then 'Sennichi' in Kume from 1962). Order the Okinawa zenzai: plump, slow-stewed beans under a triangle of hand-shaved ice.

dish: Frosted-mug root beer and curly fries
w: A&W came to Okinawa in 1963, years before mainland Japan — the 24-hour Makiminato drive-in on Route 58 is the chain's Okinawa flagship. Root beer in a frosted mug, curly fries and a burger is a rite of passage.

n: Steakhouse 88 Tsuji Honten (ステーキハウス88 辻本店)
w: Flagship of the Steakhouse 88 chain, descended from 'CLUB88', an A-sign restaurant licensed for US personnel in 1955. Neon diner room, 20-plus steak cuts, open till 1 am — the classic Okinawan 'shime' (end-of-night) steak.

dish: Sanmainiku soba and aasa (sea-lettuce) soba with house-made noodles
w: Roadside soba house near Manza Beach: preservative-free house noodles, a light but bonito-rich broth and pork belly that falls apart at a touch; the aasa soba works sea lettuce into both noodles and topping.
A newer-generation Naha soba shop that made both the Okinawa Times 900-reader noodle poll and Okinawa Traveler's five soba shops locals recommend with confidence.

dish: Okinawa soba in three noodles (classic, soy-milk, seaweed) with bonito broth
address: 1172 Ōgan, Yaese, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
w: Soba served in a registered cultural-property red-tiled house; choose classic, soy-milk or seaweed noodles in a light but deep bonito broth.

address: Southern Okinawa main island, Okinawa, Japan
w: Southern soba shop picked both in the Okinawa Times 2023 noodle-lovers' poll (south edition) and by Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five.
A century-old Okinawan farmhouse compound in the hills above Nago serving soki soba and agu pork; one of Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five and on Stars and Stripes' soba trail.

dish: Zenzai (brown-sugar kintoki beans under shaved ice)
w: Motobu's half-century-old zenzai shop that does exactly one thing: sweet stewed red kidney beans buried under a peak of shaved ice, bought with a ticket from the door.

dish: Okinawa soba and Ryukyu home cooking
n: Shima-jikan, Onna (沖縄料理の店 島時間)
w: Onna village Okinawan kitchen certified by Okinawa Prefecture as a 'restaurant where you can taste Ryukyu cuisine' and picked in Okinawa Traveler's soba round-up.

n: Inaka Ryōri no Mise Kura, Miyako (田舎料理の店 蔵)
w: Country-cooking izakaya in Hirara using island miso in champuru and rafute; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and a Mapple guidebook pick.

dish: Duru-ten (taro croquette, invented here) with awamori from every distillery
n: Urizun (古酒と琉球料理 うりずん)
w: Opened 15 August 1972 by gathering bottles from every awamori distillery in Okinawa — the bar that brought awamori back to the people. Order duru-ten, the fried taro croquette Okinawa Times traces to this kitchen, and a flight of kūsu (aged awamori).
